name: SatsGuard
tagline: Offline Bitcoin PSBT intent checks, with a redacted evidence report.
trackSaveStatus: Checkbox selected and Save clicked, but no track chip visible; must verify before publish.
problem:
## The proposal should match the promise
A Bitcoin PSBT can contain the right-looking fee while sending funds to an unintended script. Uploading it to an explorer or remote decoder also reveals transaction and wallet metadata.

SatsGuard is a local, read-only preflight for humans and agent tooling. Paste a real BIP174 PSBT v0 (base64 or hex), declare each recipient and exact satoshi amount, explicitly allow change addresses, and set an absolute fee cap. The shared browser/CLI engine compares decoded output scripts and aggregated payment totals, shows where every output goes, and flags undeclared destinations, payment mismatches, excessive or unknown supplied fees, and privacy metadata.

The redacted JSON report excludes addresses, scripts, outpoints, public keys, derivation values and the raw PSBT. Amounts and transaction shape remain. No accounts, remote APIs, analytics, keys, signing or broadcasting are used by the app.

Four synthetic testnet scenarios reproduce a recipient swap, matched intent, a fee spike, and missing input values. The core has 24 passing regression tests; actual Edge QA includes offline operation after load and a mobile layout.

**Limits:** Input values are PSBT claims, not chain-verified balances. Change ownership, signatures, spending scripts, spendability and chain state are unverified. PSBT v2 and exact final fee-rate calculation are unsupported. A result is not approval to sign.

**Built for BOSS Battle on Oct 5, 2026 with OpenAI Codex AI assistance.** Original policy engine/UI/tests/fixtures; bitcoinjs-lib 7.0.1 handles protocol parsing. Cypherpunk track: keep sensitive proposals local and make metadata exposure visible.
challenges:
The hardest part was avoiding a reassuring report from incomplete data. If even one input lacks a supplied UTXO amount, the fee is unknown and the cap cannot pass. Conflicting witness/non-witness claims are blocked; supplied previous transactions must match the input transaction hash and output index.

Protocol parsing alone was insufficient for this narrow contract: strict envelope checks reject trailing bytes, malformed lengths and unsupported PSBT versions. Tests keep Bitcoin transaction version 2 distinct from PSBT version 2.

Address text and output position cannot establish intent or change ownership. SatsGuard compares decoded scripts, aggregates repeated recipients, and accepts change only from an explicit allowlist. Exact integer satoshi arithmetic is shared with the CLI.

A separate review found two metadata-counting bugs; both were corrected and covered by regressions. Redaction uses an export allowlist, and edited form inputs disable stale report exports. These are tested prototype checks, not a professional security audit.
